source_text: Quod certe tanto peius est, quanto gravius est studium malorum quam neglectus bonorum, quanto perniciosior intentio profanitatis quam dubitatio veritatis, quanto postremo scelestius est audere criminari Deum quam nolle venerari.
pass_a_gloss: Which certainly is so much worse as the pursuit of evils is heavier than neglect of goods, as the intention of profanity is more destructive than doubt of truth, as finally it is more wicked to dare to accuse God than to be unwilling to venerate him.

lemmas.lexica: LS bonum; Blaise good-of-nature vs good-of-will
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: This is worse by as much as the pursuit of evil is worse than neglect of good, as deliberate irreverence is more destructive than doubt about the truth, and, finally, as daring to accuse God is more wicked than refusing to worship him.

choices.why: Loaded word in Julian's Latin at this locus; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
